constraints.name: Availability
constraints.injunction: Never treat freshwater as an abundant resource by default in a recommendation.

constraints.name: Quality
constraints.statement: Clean water is rarer than water itself.
constraints.injunction: Never count an available water volume without specifying its quality level and possible use.

constraints.name: Variability
constraints.statement: Rainfall patterns shift; cycles become distorted.
constraints.injunction: Do not rely on historically stable precipitation series for long-term water planning.

constraints.name: Natural Storage
constraints.injunction: Never present natural water reservoirs as stable or permanent stocks in a recommendation.

constraints.name: Pollution
constraints.injunction: Flag the asymmetry between contamination speed and restoration speed in any water-related proposal.

constraints.name: Competition
constraints.injunction: Make explicit the trade-offs between competing uses rather than assuming simultaneous availability for all.

constraints.name: Evaporation
constraints.injunction: Include increased evaporation losses under warming in any water balance estimate.

constraints.name: Droughts
constraints.statement: They are becoming longer and more frequent.
constraints.injunction: Do not rely on historical drought frequency to assess future risk.

constraints.name: Floods
constraints.statement: Too much water can mean no drinking water at all.
constraints.injunction: Systematically distinguish water quantity from available drinking water in flood analysis.

constraints.name: Water Justice
constraints.injunction: Account for the equity and power dimension of water access in any policy or recommendation.
